title: Draw a Manga Eye
steps: Lightly sketch a tilted almond shape for the eye outline.
Add a thick upper lash line and a thinner lower line.
Draw a large iris circle that touches the top lash.
Place one big highlight and one small highlight in the iris.
Shade the iris darker at the top and lighter at the bottom.
tips: Keep the highlights clean and unshaded to make the eye feel alive.

title: Draw a Simple Manga Nose and Mouth
steps: Mark a short center guideline for face symmetry.
Place a tiny angled mark for the nose near the face center.
Draw a short curved line for a relaxed manga smile.
Add a second subtle line under the mouth for the lower lip hint.
Erase extra guide marks so the features stay clean and minimal.
tips: In manga style, less detail on the nose and mouth often looks better.

title: Draw a Chibi Head
steps: Sketch a large circle for the cranium.
Add a small jaw shape under the circle for a cute face base.
Draw a vertical and horizontal guideline cross on the face.
Place oversized eyes below the horizontal guide and a tiny mouth.
Add simple bangs and erase guide lines.
tips: A chibi head usually looks best when the eyes take up lots of space.

title: Draw a Chibi Body Pose
steps: Draw a short bean-like torso under your chibi head.
Add simple tube arms and legs with rounded ends.
Pose one arm up and one leg forward for motion.
Sketch oversized sleeves and short boots.
Refine the silhouette with confident final lines.
tips: Keep limbs short and chunky to preserve the chibi look.

title: Draw Manga Hair Strands
steps: Block in the full hair shape like a helmet around the head.
Split the shape into big strand groups starting at the part.
Add pointed strand tips with quick curved strokes.
Ink the outer silhouette thicker than inner strand lines.
Shade under bangs and near roots to create depth.
tips: Think in big strand groups first, then add a few detail lines.

title: Draw Manga Speed Lines
steps: Pick a focal point where the action is happening.
Use a ruler to draw long lines radiating from that point.
Vary spacing so some areas are dense and others open.
Thicken a few key lines to increase impact.
Leave the character area clearer so the figure stays readable.
tips: Speed lines work best when they support the character, not cover them.

title: Draw a Manga Action Panel
steps: Sketch a tilted panel border for dramatic composition.
Place a dynamic stick figure line-of-action through the frame.
Build the character over that line with rough body forms.
Add impact effects like burst shapes and debris marks.
Ink final contours and keep the background minimal for focus.
tips: A strong line-of-action makes even simple poses feel energetic.

title: Draw Manga Expressions Sheet
steps: Draw four matching face circles in a grid.
Add the same eye placement guides in each face.
Draw happy, angry, sad, and surprised eyebrow shapes.
Change eye and mouth shapes to match each emotion.
Clean lines and label each expression for practice review.
tips: Keep the head structure consistent so emotion changes are easier to compare.
